assessments.reasoning: Ada 2022 §12.1 places a generic formal part before the package specification in a generic package declaration. The grammar permits zero parameter declarations within that part. Section 10.1 supplies the separate library-unit clause of the claim.

Ada 2022 §10.1 gives separate compilation as a defining property of library units and includes packages among their possible kinds. Together with §12.1 this supports both clauses without requiring a generic package declaration to be a library unit.

challenge.method: Read the grammar with zero repetitions after the generic keyword. Consider a package declared physically inside another program unit and distinguish it from a child library unit.
challenge.results: The formal part still occurs. A declaration with no formal parameters satisfies the claimed syntax. The manual allows physical nesting and separately recognizes logically nested library children. Separate compilation follows from library-unit status alone in this claim.

limitations: A generic formal part can contain zero generic formal parameter declarations.
A package can also be nested. This claim covers separate compilation only for packages that are library units.
Both clauses derive from the same Ada 2022 manual. No independent corroboration is asserted. The result describes grammar and the library-unit definition.
